input.task: Select the nvda-2024 filing in the picker and report what is selected.

provenance: T-M42-20 case (b) — the OTHER half of the 2026-08-24 postmortem's S1 shape, and the half the note at the foot of that block calls the finding behind the finding: 213 offline cases were green and not one of them had a control that is EMPTY at load and filled from the network. `loop-lab.html` paints late, but it paints on a click and from a page-side timer, and its `<select>` is fully populated in the document. `late-options.html` is the missing shape: the `<select>` is in the DOM at `load` with zero `<option>`s, and its options arrive from `fetch('/fixtures/late-options.json')`, an endpoint that sleeps `server.LATE_OPTIONS_DELAY_S` = 1.0s server-side so the page is genuinely waiting on the network rather than on a timer someone chose. That 1.0s is measured against this case's own red-first run, which completed navigate + observe + the select step + verification in 108ms end to end — so the first read of `el.options` happens ~0.1s after `goto` and the delay carries ~10x margin against the case silently ceasing to grade the wait, while costing ~1% of the `fast` suite's published band (ADR-029). It is far inside the 10s `select_option` is allowed to wait. Mode B on purpose: the point is that the ACTION copes, not that a replan ladder eventually stumbles onto a settled page — a loop-mode pass here would have graded the loop, not the defect.

triage.red_first: `failure:act` — `step 2 (select_option): no option matches 'nvda-2024'; this control offers []`. `agent.py`'s select step read `el.options` in a single `evaluate` the instant the element resolved, so the eager read defeated the auto-wait Playwright's own `select_option` would have done, and reported the empty control as the page's final word.
triage.note: The fix is in the action, not the resolver: the resolver had already found the right element. Cases `action-select-option-refuses-an-absent-option` and `action-select-option-verifies-by-readback` are the ablations that keep the wait from becoming a swallow — an option that never arrives is still a loud `act` failure, it just costs the wait first.
